habit_scope: Asphalt strip shingles as the FINISH covering on a pitched 2-story light-wood roof. Sheathing + eave protection / ice barrier is P09 (Logan ice is P09; Fontana does not get a Utah snow pack). CMHC Ch12: covering as soon as sheathing is in to keep the building dry — field dry-in is P09; this Method is the shingle finish with PRECEDES from P09.
how_it_is_done: P09 dry-in first: roof sheathing on; eave protection where required (CMHC: Type S or Type M roll roofing, joints lapped ≥100 mm / 4 in and cemented, OR peel-and-stick bituminous membrane). Ice dam / eave protection is P09. Logan ice barrier is on the city sheet. Fontana does not get a Utah snow pack.
Install covering as soon as sheathing is in to keep the building dry (CMHC Ch12) — that sentence is why dry-in lives P09; the shingle courses are the finish.

Starter strip: shingles with tabs removed along the eaves, extending ≥12 mm (1/2 in) beyond eaves/rakes/fascia to form a drip; OR shingle strip tabs up; OR Type M roll as starter (and as eave protection if continued up the slope). Nail starter along the bottom edge at 300 mm (12 in) intervals.
First course: butt edge in line with the bottom of the starter strip. Chalk lines for tab alignment. Asphalt-impregnated building paper often used as underlay; printed lines help alignment.
Four large-head roofing nails per strip, long enough to penetrate at least 12 mm (1/2 in) into the roof sheathing. Most asphalt shingles are self-sealing.
Normal slope 1:3 or greater. Low slope 1:6 to 1:3 needs cemented courses (CMHC) — not the habit for a typical pitched SFR; confirm AHJ. Interlocking/special: manufacturer.

Valley/step/wall flashing is P10/Ch14 already; shingles lap over flashing (Fig 125). Shingle nails must not be placed within 75 mm (3 in) of the valley centre line at the ridge, or within 125 mm (5 in) at the eaves (Ch14).
tools_equipment: Named: roofing nails; chalk line. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Eave protection / ice barrier is P09 — Logan city sheet; Fontana no Utah snow pack.
Four nails per strip, 1/2 in into sheathing (CMHC Ch12).
Starter nailed 12 in OC along the bottom edge.
Do not nail within 3 in of valley center at ridge / 5 in at eaves (Ch14).

when_this_beats_habit: This is the pitched-roof finish habit. Metal/tile/wood shakes are named alts in Ch12 — not filed this pass.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Copying Logan ice onto Fontana. Treating eave protection as optional on a Logan roof. Nailing in the valley.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They shingle. What they skip is four nails, starter 12 in, and ice as P09/Logan not a Fontana copy.
permit_gate_notes: Ice barrier: Logan city sheet / P09. Fontana no Utah snow pack. CMHC is NBC — confirm AHJ.
risk_if_swapped_late: Changing covering type after sheathing is a load/underlayment change. Tile needs an engineer (CMHC). Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Dry-in and ice are P09. This is the shingles: starter at the drip, four nails a strip into the sheathing, no nails in the valley. Do not put a Utah ice pack on a Fontana roof.
